champion.name: ema-pullback-v1
champion.hypothesis: Buy pullbacks to EMA21 in an EMA50>EMA200 uptrend when RSI is not overbought; exit on ATR stop, take-profit, or trend loss.

lastEvaluation.diagnosis:
The strategy is not just having a bad week — it is structurally broken and has been for the whole sample (prior: 233 trades, 21.0% win rate, PF 0.15; this week: 29 trades, 20.7% win rate, PF 0.11). The entry filter (pullback to EMA21 in an EMA50>EMA200 uptrend, RSI<62, volume≥0.8×avg) is not discriminating winners from losers at all: winners' avg RSI at entry is 52.66 vs losers' 51.38 — statistically indistinguishable. The only variable that separates the two groups is realised volatility: winners average vol48 = 0.00131 vs losers 0.00079, i.e. winners are entered in ~67% higher-vol conditions and are held much longer before hitting target (avg 17.5 bars) while losers are stopped out fast (avg 7.6 bars, 18/23 losers exit via stop). This points to a chop problem: in low-vol48 grind, price oscillates around EMA21 just enough to trigger the "pullback" condition, but the 1.5×ATR stop is tight enough that normal noise clips it before any directional move develops.

The stop/target asymmetry compounds this: stopAtr=1.5 vs tpAtr=3.0 (1:2 R:R) requires roughly ≥35% win rate after costs to break even, but realised win rate is 20.7% — nowhere close. One outlier trade (2026-09-04T12:15, entry 81216→exit 79832, -1.70 gross on a 3-bar hold) shows the stop can be blown through by a sharp move/gap for far more than 1.5×ATR, i.e. slippage/gap risk isn't bounded by the nominal stop distance — that single trade cost -1.90 net, ~18% of the week's total loss.

Cost drag is real but secondary to the signal problem: fees average ~$0.20/trade (0.2% on $100 notional, consistent with the 0.10% fee rate × round trip), totaling $5.80 this week against a gross P&L of -$4.55 — fees roughly double the loss, but even gross P&L alone is negative, so this is fundamentally a bad-signal / bad-exit problem, not just a costs-eating-small-edges problem. Notably several "take-profit" exits are barely profitable or net losers even before considering that the target was nominally 3×ATR away (e.g. entry 78122, ATR=36.26 → nominal TP≈78231, but exit fill was only 78167, gross +0.06, net -0.14 after fee) — the bar-close-based exit fill is landing well short of the ATR target, meaning realized favorable excursion is much smaller than the stated tpAtr assumes, effectively making the true R:R worse than 1:2.
hypotheses: Entries where vol48 < 0.0009 (below the losers' average) have a materially lower win rate than entries where vol48 ≥ 0.0013 (near winners' average), because low-vol regimes produce mean-reverting chop around EMA21 that clips the 1.5×ATR stop before trend resumes.

Widening the stop to ~2.0–2.2×ATR while shrinking the take-profit to ~2.0×ATR (closer to the realistically achievable favorable excursion seen in winning trades) will raise win rate enough to overcome the 1.5:3.0 R:R's ~35% breakeven requirement, net of the ~0.3% round-trip cost.

Adding a short-term trend-alignment filter (EMA9 > EMA21, i.e., price already turning back up, not just touching EMA21) will filter out entries into unresolved chop and raise the effective win rate closer to what the R:R requires.

variants.name: vol-filtered-conservative
variants.hypothesis: Hypothesis: entries during vol48 below ~0.0009 (chop regime) are unprofitable; restricting entries to higher realised-vol regimes plus stricter trend alignment will cut trade count sharply and raise win rate.

variants.name: wider-stop-realistic-tp
variants.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the 1.5xATR stop is too tight for entry noise (18/23 losers exit via stop, avg hold only 7.6 bars); widening the stop and shrinking the take-profit toward the realistically achievable move will raise net win rate and expectancy.

variants.name: momentum-confirmed-entry
variants.hypothesis: Hypothesis: requiring an actual bullish confirmation candle (close>open) plus a minimum vol48 floor, instead of merely being near EMA21, filters out chop-driven false pullbacks and raises win rate above the R:R breakeven threshold.
